Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea Dishwasher 12-Person, White, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, Installation Room User - Couple in their 30s + 5-Year-Old Child. Finally, we have a dishwasher aunt in our home. These days, I'm truly experiencing why we call it "aunt, aunt"—a dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill it to the brim and run it once a day, and I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into this dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money—I think the price is definitely the best! Considering a 12-person machine costs at least a million won, I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. However, after using it every day, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write this down below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance is that different! 2 Performance - As I wrote above, it washes dishes very well. I had two questions while using the Mydia dishwasher. 1. Why are there still water marks? I used the most famous and good detergent, but I had a question, so I looked it up and it said, 'When washing at high temperatures and drying quickly, limescale such as minerals in the water can remain on the surface of the dishes, causing white marks or water marks.' I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid because I heard that it definitely reduces or eliminates water marks if you use a rinse aid, but I heard that putting vinegar in the rinse aid compartment is one way to do it, so I'm going to give it a try and think about it! 2. As I wrote about the fishy smell of water, I only felt the fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit disgusting. Before I brought in the dishwasher, I used to wash the dishes with the hottest water while wearing rubber gloves, but the standard mode of the dishwasher was lukewarm compared to the water temperature I usually wash dishes with. So, I turned it on high temperature and there was no smell at all! This part was also neatly resolved. Conclusion: After turning it on once a day, the course I have settled on now is [High temperature wash - automatic door opening]. When I set it like this, it takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes. I did not set the drying separately, but after it was finished, I took it out in steps and let it dry naturally, and it dried well! There was no smell, maybe because I washed it with hot water! And on the first shelf, which is the lowest shelf, I put pots and pans, large bowls, cutting boards, etc. On the second shelf, I put plates, regular bowls, cups, etc. On the third shelf, I keep scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks and rotate them. Since there are three of us, I rotate all the dishes we use for the day at once after dinner, which is perfect! It's really nice because I have less time for housework and I have more free time. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

These days, I'm truly experiencing why we call it "aunt, aunt"—a dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). Value for money—I think the price is definitely the best! Considering a 12-person machine costs at least a million won, I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. However, after using it every day, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write this down below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance is that different! 2 Performance - As I wrote above, it washes dishes very well. I had two questions while using the Mydia dishwasher. 1. Why are there still water marks? I used the most famous and good detergent, but I had a question, so I looked it up and it said, 'When washing at high temperatures and drying quickly, limescale such as minerals in the water can remain on the surface of the dishes, causing white marks or water marks.' I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid because I heard that it definitely reduces or eliminates water marks if you use a rinse aid, but I heard that putting vinegar in the rinse aid compartment is one way to do it, so I'm going to give it a try and think about it! 2. As I wrote about the fishy smell of water, I only felt the fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit disgusting. Before I brought in the dishwasher, I used to wash the dishes with the hottest water while wearing rubber gloves, but the standard mode of the dishwasher was lukewarm compared to the water temperature I usually wash dishes with. So, I turned it on high temperature and there was no smell at all! This part was also neatly resolved. Conclusion: After turning it on once a day, the course I have settled on now is [High temperature wash - automatic door opening]. When I set it like this, it takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes. I did not set the drying separately, but after it was finished, I took it out in steps and let it dry naturally, and it dried well! There was no smell, maybe because I washed it with hot water! Since there are three of us, I rotate all the dishes we use for the day at once after dinner, which is perfect! It's really nice because I have less time for housework and I have more free time. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Since there are three of us, I rotate all the dishes we use for the day at once after dinner, which is perfect! It's really nice because I have less time for housework and I have more free time. MyDea Dishwasher 12-Person, White, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, Installation Room User - Couple in their 30s + 5-Year-Old Child. Finally, we have a dishwasher aunt in our home. These days, I'm truly experiencing why we call it "aunt, aunt"—a dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill it to the brim and run it once a day, and I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into this dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money—I think the price is definitely the best! Considering a 12-person machine costs at least a million won, I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. However, after using it every day, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write this down below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance is that different! 2 Performance - As I wrote above, it washes dishes very well. I had two questions while using the Mydia dishwasher. 1. Why are there still water marks? I used the most famous and good detergent, but I had a question, so I looked it up and it said, 'When washing at high temperatures and drying quickly, limescale such as minerals in the water can remain on the surface of the dishes, causing white marks or water marks.' I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid because I heard that it definitely reduces or eliminates water marks if you use a rinse aid, but I heard that putting vinegar in the rinse aid compartment is one way to do it, so I'm going to give it a try and think about it! 2. As I wrote about the fishy smell of water, I only felt the fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit disgusting. Before I brought in the dishwasher, I used to wash the dishes with the hottest water while wearing rubber gloves, but the standard mode of the dishwasher was lukewarm compared to the water temperature I usually wash dishes with. So, I turned it on high temperature and there was no smell at all! This part was also neatly resolved. Conclusion: After turning it on once a day, the course I have settled on now is [High temperature wash - automatic door opening]. When I set it like this, it takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes. I did not set the drying separately, but after it was finished, I took it out in steps and let it dry naturally, and it dried well! There was no smell, maybe because I washed it with hot water! And on the first shelf, which is the lowest shelf, I put pots and pans, large bowls, cutting boards, etc. On the second shelf, I put plates, regular bowls, cups, etc. On the third shelf, I keep scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks and rotate them. Since there are three of us, I rotate all the dishes we use for the day at once after dinner, which is perfect! It's really nice because I have less time for housework and I have more free time. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea Dishwasher 12-Person, White, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, Installation Room User - Couple in their 30s + 5-Year-Old Child. Finally, we have a dishwasher aunt in our home. These days, I'm truly experiencing why we call it "aunt, aunt"—a dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill it to the brim and run it once a day, and I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into this dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money—I think the price is definitely the best! Considering a 12-person machine costs at least a million won, I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. However, after using it every day, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write this down below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance is that different! 2 Performance - As I wrote above, it washes dishes very well. I had two questions while using the Mydia dishwasher. 1. Why are there still water marks? I used the most famous and good detergent, but I had a question, so I looked it up and it said, 'When washing at high temperatures and drying quickly, limescale such as minerals in the water can remain on the surface of the dishes, causing white marks or water marks.' I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid because I heard that it definitely reduces or eliminates water marks if you use a rinse aid, but I heard that putting vinegar in the rinse aid compartment is one way to do it, so I'm going to give it a try and think about it! 2. As I wrote about the fishy smell of water, I only felt the fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit disgusting. Before I brought in the dishwasher, I used to wash the dishes with the hottest water while wearing rubber gloves, but the standard mode of the dishwasher was lukewarm compared to the water temperature I usually wash dishes with. So, I turned it on high temperature and there was no smell at all! This part was also neatly resolved. Conclusion: After turning it on once a day, the course I have settled on now is [High temperature wash - automatic door opening]. When I set it like this, it takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes. I did not set the drying separately, but after it was finished, I took it out in steps and let it dry naturally, and it dried well! There was no smell, maybe because I washed it with hot water! And on the first shelf, which is the lowest shelf, I put pots and pans, large bowls, cutting boards, etc. On the second shelf, I put plates, regular bowls, cups, etc. On the third shelf, I keep scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks and rotate them. Since there are three of us, I rotate all the dishes we use for the day at once after dinner, which is perfect! It's really nice because I have less time for housework and I have more free time. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea Dishwasher 12-Person, White, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, Installation Room User - Couple in their 30s + 5-Year-Old Child. Finally, we have a dishwasher aunt in our home. These days, I'm truly experiencing why we call it "aunt, aunt"—a dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill it to the brim and run it once a day, and I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into this dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money—I think the price is definitely the best! Considering a 12-person machine costs at least a million won, I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. However, after using it every day, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write this down below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance is that different! 2 Performance - As I wrote above, it washes dishes very well. I had two questions while using the Mydia dishwasher. 1. Why are there still water marks? I used the most famous and good detergent, but I had a question, so I looked it up and it said, 'When washing at high temperatures and drying quickly, limescale such as minerals in the water can remain on the surface of the dishes, causing white marks or water marks.' I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid because I heard that it definitely reduces or eliminates water marks if you use a rinse aid, but I heard that putting vinegar in the rinse aid compartment is one way to do it, so I'm going to give it a try and think about it! 2. As I wrote about the fishy smell of water, I only felt the fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit disgusting. Before I brought in the dishwasher, I used to wash the dishes with the hottest water while wearing rubber gloves, but the standard mode of the dishwasher was lukewarm compared to the water temperature I usually wash dishes with. So, I turned it on high temperature and there was no smell at all! This part was also neatly resolved. Conclusion: After turning it on once a day, the course I have settled on now is [High temperature wash - automatic door opening]. When I set it like this, it takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes. I did not set the drying separately, but after it was finished, I took it out in steps and let it dry naturally, and it dried well! There was no smell, maybe because I washed it with hot water! And on the first shelf, which is the lowest shelf, I put pots and pans, large bowls, cutting boards, etc. On the second shelf, I put plates, regular bowls, cups, etc. On the third shelf, I keep scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks and rotate them. Since there are three of us, I rotate all the dishes we use for the day at once after dinner, which is perfect! It's really nice because I have less time for housework and I have more free time. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): I'ts nice and works but there are a few features missing that I thought it had and I could have gotten on a cheaper dishwasher, even a cheaper Bosch.
Comments (English): I'ts nice and works but there are a few features missing that I thought it had and I could have gotten on a cheaper dishwasher, even a cheaper Bosch. One is automatic door opening at the end of the program (If I just haven't found how to do it then someone from Bosch please contact me about it). The door can automatically open when you push against it so why not at the end of the program. The second is the time display. It doesn't display the remaining time on the floor and the screen is hidden as it's an integrated dishwasher. You have to get your phone out to see the remaining time on the app (which is hard to navigate and use). The last gripe is the power plug, It could just be an Australian thing but why do appliance manufactures insist on supplying ugly space wasting straight plastic plugs. Especially for something like a dishwasher where the power point will be behind or in a cupboard where space is precious. Maybe small things for some but it's the most expensive Bosch you can buy here and you basically have to buy one blind as no one has a display one to actually see. The last Bosch I had was 17 years old when I sold the house so I have no doubt this one will do the job, I just wanted the fruit too.

Sentence (English): This review was written after receiving a free product as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (English): [ Very good ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. The My Dear 12-seater dishwasher. I no longer play rock-paper-scissors over dishes. Hey, you know what we said most during our first year of marriage? "Honey, who's going to do the dishes?" "Who put the dirty dishes in?" "But where are we now?" We both put our dishes in the dishwasher and do our own thing. I got the chance to try this product out as a Coupang Experience Group member (and used it for about two weeks). I used to have back pain, so standing up to do dishes was incredibly difficult. Since getting the My Dear dishwasher, my back has improved so much! Oh! And Coupang's installation is amazing. I was so surprised when it was installed the next day after I ordered. I placed my order in the evening, and the next morning, they knocked on my door, thinking it was a delivery. "Is this your dishwasher?" This product can be built-in or freestanding. Johee's house is freestanding! Because it's a lease. Kitchen interior? There's no such thing. But it looks great even when set up separately. I used to put new cabinets in it, but I don't think that's necessary. It's a large 12-person unit! Pots, frying pans, plates, and even baby dishes piled up for three meals all fit in one room. It's three-tiered, so spoons and forks are on top, plates in the middle, and pots on the bottom. They stack up neatly and easily! The highlight is the automatic door opening function! When it's done, the door opens by itself with a "pop!" At first, I'd run over, thinking, "Honey! Why is it open?" But now, even that's cute. When I see the dishes fluffing up as they release steam, I'm just so touched that I pat them. Conclusion: This is the real deal. It's cost-effective, has great cleaning power, is easy to install, and has an automatic door opening. It even has app control, so if I forget to turn it on, I can control it from outside! Before, I lost peace of mind while washing dishes, but now I've found peace in front of the dishwasher. Who washes dishes by hand these days?! We just trust the machine and sit back and watch dramas. (And I'm so touched by the sound of the door opening that I'm looking at it again^^). It's a bit big, so it might not fit the height of a sink in an apartment or villa, but it can also be used as a freestanding unit, so consider it!

As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda).
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won.
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands?
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

(I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!
