A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!
Comments (English): [ I understand why everyone is using the dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. MyDea dishwasher, 12-seater, white, MDWEF1233G(W)-KR, on-site installation. Actual user - Couple in their 30s with a 5-year-old child. We finally have a dishwasher aunt in our home. A dryer, a robot vacuum cleaner, and finally, a dishwasher. These days, I'm truly experiencing why they call it "aunt, aunt." As soon as I received the dishwasher, I stocked up on ProX detergent (basic, baking soda). I usually fill the dishwasher to the brim and run it once a day. I use the standard-sized detergents one at a time, without cutting them. Let's delve into the dishwasher review in more detail. 1. Value for money. The price is definitely top-notch! A 12-seater machine costs at least a million won. I wondered if the performance was so good at such a low price. But in daily use, I've only had one complaint about the dishwasher's performance! (I'll write about this below!) This brand washes dishes this well, so how much better are expensive brands? I don't think the performance difference is that big! 2. Performance. As I mentioned above, it washes dishes incredibly well. I had two questions while using my Mydia dishwasher. 1. Water stains. Why on earth were water stains still there? I used the most famous and recommended detergent, but... I was curious and looked into it. It said, "During the high-temperature washing and rapid drying process, limescale, such as minerals in the water, can remain on the surface of the dishes, leaving white marks or water stains." I was wondering if I should buy a rinse aid, as I was told that using a rinse aid would definitely reduce or eliminate the stains. But... I heard adding vinegar to the rinse aid compartment is one solution. I'll give it a try and see if it helps! 2. Fishy smell. As I mentioned above, I've only had a fishy smell once while using ProX baking soda, and it was a bit gross. Even when I was washing dishes regularly before I bought the dishwasher. I used to wash dishes with rubber gloves on and the hottest water possible, but the dishwasher's standard mode was lukewarm, even warmer than my usual dishwashing water. So I tried running it on high, and there was no smell at all! This problem was solved. Conclusion: After running it once a day, I've settled on the [High Temperature Wash - Auto Door Open] cycle. It takes about an hour and a half with this setting. I don't have a separate drying setting; I just take the dishes out on the steps after they're done and let them air dry. They dry well! Perhaps because I wash them in hot water, there's no smell! Also, I keep pots, pans, large bowls, and cutting boards on the first rack, the lowest rack. Plates, regular dishes, and cups are on the second rack. And scissors, knives, and children's chopsticks are almost always on the third rack. For a family of three, it's perfect to run all the dishes I've used for the day in one go after dinner! It's so nice to have less time for housework and more time to relax. Auntie, the dishwasher is the best!

Sentence (English): This is the product I chose for my first foray into dishwashers, based on recommendations from people around me.
Comments (English): This is the product I chose for my first foray into dishwashers, based on recommendations from people around me. Well, as everyone already knows, you can pretty much assume that all the small and medium-sized brands in Korea are products of this company. They just release products under different brand names, so it’s not a manufacturer with inferior quality. While looking up reviews on YouTube, I discovered that this product used to be sold under the SK Magic brand. Above all else, I’m a mint color enthusiast, so I chose this one because it was the only mint-colored option available. I also wanted a slim design. Using it for the first time, it washes surprisingly well. However, perhaps because I’m not used to it yet, arranging the dishes like Tetris is quite difficult. As a single-person household, there are moments when I have a moment of realization: "Ah, at this rate, I could just hand-wash it and it would be done in no time." Since it is slim by default, it is on the taller side, but the top basket is removable, so you can wash taller items as well. But did this product not have a drying function? The manual lists "drying" at the end of the cycle, but it seems to just be natural drying. There doesn't seem to be a separate drying mode or a fan function. Anyway, the mint color is so pretty. The kitchen is especially small, so I removed the old drying rack and put this one in its place. But the drying rack keeps lingering in my mind. Even with a dishwasher, I feel like I need a drying rack. Ah. And where am I supposed to put that?

Sentence (English): This dishwasher easily accepts 1.5 times the amount of dishes typical dishwashers do.
Comments (English): [ Amazing large capacity dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher easily accepts 1.5 times the amount of dishes typical dishwashers do. If you like entertaining people and find yourself struggling in accommodating all the items in the dishwasher, this one is for you! The large 3rd rack can fit many big sized bowls and many mugs and glasses. It also has its own dedicated water spray. The cutlery basket is huge, and can be detached to make it more reasonably sized and use the freed up space to fit another pan. There are many cycle options and the drying cycle is pretty effective. The noise level is very low and won't bother you at all. At this price point, we had a choice between a Bosch and this one. Despite several stellar reviews for the Bosch's performance and durability, we went with this one, and so far feel that it's been the right choice. The only gripe we have is around the fact there is no status indicator on the front and there is no way to find out if it's running or not. At this price point, a WiFi chip and smart features would have been appreciated. All in all, a great dishwasher.

After two weeks I came across the instructions pamphlet and read that the middle rack is adjustable up so I did that and voila! I can add my plates.
